answer: Jittered arrival corridors. Each identity must submit its first N actions through a randomly assigned arrival window, checked against a per-agent timing profile; bursts outside the window are shed. Honest agents drift like a zephyr, spreading load smoothly. Sybil fleets spin up in synchronized waves, so each extra identity collides with the corridor edge and must be re-queued through a slow lagoon of delay. A canyon of queue depth opens: attackers pay wall-clock time per identity, scaling linearly with fleet size while honest cost stays flat.
